"Act as a Lead Game Designer. Create a detailed Game Design Document (GDD) concept for a hardcore off-road simulator combining the terrain physics and logistics of *SnowRunner* with the mechanical tuning depth and domestic vehicle roster of *UAZ 4x4: Complete Drive (Полный привод)*.

Core Requirements:
1. Deformable Terrain @COMMENT_BODY@ Physics: Dynamic mud, peat bogs, snow, water current drag, winching physics, and realistic component damage/wear.
2. Granular Mechanical Tuning (UAZ 4x4 Style):
   - Axles @COMMENT_BODY@ Drivetrain: Military portal axles (\"военные мосты\"), differential lockers, crawler transfer-case ratios, reinforced half-shafts.
   - Wheels @COMMENT_BODY@ Tires: On-the-fly tire pressure deflation (CTIS), beadlocks, extreme bogger treads, tire chains.
   - Off-Road Prep: Snorkels, sealed ignition, relocated radiators, suspension lifts (spring-over-axle), and high-amp winches.
3. Vehicle Lineup: Rugged utility 4x4s and cab-over trucks inspired by UAZ-469, UAZ-452 \"Bukhanka\", VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
4. Gameplay Loop: Taiga trail scouting, technical low-gear rock/mud crawling, field maintenance, and vehicle recovery missions.

Deliverable: Provide the core drivetrain simulation specs, a complete garage upgrade tree for a starter scout 4x4, and the mission structure for the first 3 hours of gameplay.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Field manual

FIELD GUIDE 01—06

Traction is a conversation
with the ground.

TAIGA is a slow, systemic off-road simulation. The terrain remembers every pass; the truck remembers every mistake.

DESIGN PILLAR 01WEIGHT · GRIP · CONSEQUENCE
SIMULATION SPEC 01 / DRIVETRAIN

Torque, not horsepower.

A fixed-step, wheel-level model prioritizes controllable torque delivery. Each wheel samples local ground state and feeds load, slip, and damage back into the chassis.

01

Powertrain

Engine torque curve → clutch slip → 4-speed gearbox → selectable high/low transfer case → open / locked differentials → axle reduction → tyre contact patch. Low range multiplies wheel torque 2.7× and caps road speed.

ENGINE BRAKING · CLUTCH HEAT · STALL / RESTART
02

Axles & lockers

Stock civilian axles; military portal axles add +90 mm clearance with greater unsprung mass. Lockers force axle-wheel speed parity; binding on hard turns raises shaft stress. Reinforced half-shafts raise torque threshold.

OPEN → REAR LOCK → FRONT + REAR LOCK
03

Tyres & pressure

CTIS lowers pressure on the move: more footprint and flotation, but more heat, rolling drag, and bead risk. Beadlocks widen safe pressure range. Chains add snow / ice bite, reduce soft-ground flotation.

30 PSI ROAD · 18 PSI MIXED · 8 PSI BOG (LOCKED RIMS)
04

Terrain & water

Wheel load deforms a moisture-dependent soil grid. Rut depth raises drag; wheelspin polishes mud into slick clay. Peat has a shear-strength limit and can swallow a stopped vehicle. Flowing water adds lateral force and drag.

SNORKEL PROTECTS INTAKE · NOT ELECTRICS OR CABIN
05

Damage & wear

Impacts stress suspension and chassis; high RPM in mud heats clutch and engine; submerged ignition misfires. Tyre cuts bleed pressure. Field repair consumes parts and time; recovery costs cash and abandons optional cargo.

COMPONENTS: ENGINE · COOLING · AXLES · TYRES · FRAME
06

Winching

Choose an anchor, pay cable out, tension rises against vehicle mass and terrain suction. Line angle matters; trees can uproot. A high-amp winch pulls harder but draws battery current—engine off means finite reserve.

ANCHOR · CABLE · LOAD · MOTOR HEAT · BATTERY
DOMESTIC FLEET 06 CHASSIS

## Objective
- Create a playable off-road simulator prototype inspired by SnowRunner and UAZ 4x4: Complete Drive, centered on taiga trail driving, mechanical upgrades, and recovery gameplay.
- Deliver a browser-based concept build with a garage upgrade tree, mission flow, terrain-state simulation, and vehicle HUD.

## Requirements
- Hardcore off-road simulation with deformable terrain effects: mud, peat bogs, snow, water current drag, winching, and component wear.
- Granular tuning across drivetrain, wheels, and prep systems inspired by military/utility 4x4s.
- Vehicle lineup inspired by UAZ-469, UAZ-452 Bukhanka, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Gameplay loop: taiga scouting, low-gear technical crawling, field maintenance, and recovery.
- No clarifying questions; use reasonable assumptions and keep the build playable.

## Decisions
- Built a lightweight single-page browser prototype instead of a full 3D production title, to keep the project playable and self-contained in the repo.
- Modeled the core loop around a top-down driving scene with simplified terrain sampling, upgradeable vehicle stats, and scripted missions.
- Used a UAZ-469 style starter scout as the first vehicle and focused the garage on low-range, differential locking, CTIS, winching, and prep upgrades.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the interactive game shell and UI in `index.html`.
- Added the visual styling and responsive layout in `style.css`.
- Implemented the terrain, vehicle physics, HUD, mission logic, winch/CTIS controls, and workshop upgrade tree in `game.js`.
- Included a starter mission flow, map, recovery prompt, and field-repair system.
- Added a garage upgrade system with drivetrain, wheel, and prep categories.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Decide whether the project should remain a playable prototype or be expanded into a more formal GDD/spec document with structured sections and deeper lore.
2. If continuing as a game, expand the mission arc, add more vehicles, and improve terrain fidelity and tuning depth.
3. Validate the prototype in the browser and tune balance for terrain traction, damage, and recovery flow.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: main game screen, HUD, garage/workshop, and mission UI.
- `style.css`: game styling, responsive layout, and visual presentation.
- `game.js`: gameplay simulation, vehicle state, terrain sample logic, upgrade system, and mission logic.

## Important Context
- The current build is a single-page top-down off-road prototype rather than a full 3D simulation or polished production GDD.
- The mechanic and mission loop are oriented around a starter UAZ-469 style scout and the first operational chapter in a taiga environment.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser prototype combining SnowRunner-style terrain and logistics with UAZ-style mechanical tuning and domestic vehicles.
- Deliver a garage upgrade tree, drivetrain simulation specifications, and a first-three-hours mission structure through the game experience.

## Requirements
- Include mud, peat bogs, snow, water currents, winching, and component damage/wear.
- Include granular tuning for portal axles, lockers, crawler gearing, reinforced shafts, CTIS, beadlocks, bogger tires, chains, snorkels, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lifts, and winches.
- Feature vehicles inspired by the UAZ-469, UAZ-452, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Support taiga scouting, low-gear crawling, field maintenance, and recovery gameplay.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, single-page top-down browser prototype rather than a full 3D production game.
- Center gameplay on a UAZ-469-style scout, terrain sampling, mission stops, and workshop upgrades.
- Include simulation specifications, a vehicle roster, and a three-hour field plan in the in-game Field Manual.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built field, workshop, and Field Manual views in `index.html`, with responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented controls, terrain sampling, mission objectives, telemetry, upgrades, repairs, winch, and recovery UI in `game.js`.
- Added terrain color sampling, drivetrain/AWD/differential/low-pressure traction influences, and water-related engine and chassis wear.
- `node --check game.js` passed; Chromium checks confirmed navigation, vehicle movement, upgrade purchase/cash/spec updates, and mission progress.

### Active
- Continue browser validation and resolve gameplay/UI issues, especially recovery, winch, component effects, and mission progression.
- Review requested vehicle roster and first-three-hours plan against the Field Manual.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test terrain transitions, recovery, winch, repairs, CTIS, upgrade effects, and full mission progression in Chromium.
2. Fix issues found, including the recovery placeholder and topographic-map placeholder if they remain in scope.
3. Recheck syntax and browser errors, then summarize prototype scope and simplifications.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface, workshop, mission UI, and Field Manual.
- `game.js`: Simulation, controls, terrain sampling, upgrades, mission logic, and UI behavior.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and visual styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- `game.js` currently has a winch pull toward the active mission stop; an attempted edit did not apply, so the existing implementation remains.
- Recovery currently only displays “Recovery hook reached — reposition and retry.”
- `mapToggle` currently only displays “TOPO MAP OPENED.”
- Prototype is a simplified 2D top-down simulation, not production-grade deformable 3D physics.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser prototype combining SnowRunner-style terrain and logistics with UAZ-style mechanical tuning and domestic vehicles.
- Deliver a garage upgrade tree, drivetrain simulation specifications, and a first-three-hours mission structure through the game experience.

## Requirements
- Include mud, peat bogs, snow, water currents, winching, and component damage/wear.
- Include granular tuning for portal axles, lockers, crawler gearing, reinforced shafts, CTIS, beadlocks, bogger tires, chains, snorkels, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lifts, and winches.
- Feature vehicles inspired by the UAZ-469, UAZ-452, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Support taiga scouting, low-gear crawling, field maintenance, and recovery gameplay.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, single-page top-down browser prototype rather than a full 3D production game.
- Center gameplay on a UAZ-469-style scout, terrain sampling, mission stops, and workshop upgrades.
- Include simulation specifications, a vehicle roster, and a three-hour field plan in the in-game Field Manual.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built field, workshop, and Field Manual views in `index.html`, with responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented controls, terrain sampling, mission objectives, telemetry, upgrades, repairs, winch, and recovery UI in `game.js`.
- Added terrain color sampling, drivetrain/AWD/differential/low-pressure traction influences, and water-related engine and chassis wear.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest edits; Chromium checks confirmed navigation, vehicle movement, upgrade purchase/cash/spec updates, and mission progress.
- Began revising winch behavior to pull toward a selected anchor rather than the mission stop; added `state.winchAnchor` and a nearest-road-point helper.

### Active
- Finish and validate winch/recovery behavior; the new anchor state is not yet wired to the winch control.
- Continue browser validation of terrain transitions, repairs, CTIS, upgrade effects, and full mission progression.
- Review whether the Field Manual actually includes the requested vehicle roster and first-three-hours plan.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire winch activation to a suitable anchor and implement a functional recovery action; replace the topographic-map placeholder if in scope.
2. Recheck water-damage behavior after the latest edit, then run `node --check game.js` and browser validation.
3. Review the vehicle roster and first-three-hours plan in the Field Manual; fill any gaps.
4. Summarize prototype scope and simplifications after testing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface, workshop, mission UI, and Field Manual.
- `game.js`: Simulation, controls, terrain sampling, upgrades, winch, recovery, and mission logic.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and visual styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- `game.js` now has `findNearestRoadPoint()` and a `state.winchAnchor` field, but the winch button still only toggles `winchActive`; its new anchor-based pull cannot work until an anchor is assigned.
- Recovery currently only displays “Recovery hook reached — reposition and retry.”
- `mapToggle` currently only displays “TOPO MAP OPENED.”
- Prototype is a simplified 2D top-down simulation, not production-grade deformable 3D physics.

- Include granular tuning for portal axles, lockers, crawler gearing, reinforced shafts, CTIS, beadlocks, bogger tires, chains, snorkels, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lifts, and winches.
- Feature vehicles inspired by the UAZ-469, UAZ-452, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Support taiga scouting, low-gear crawling, field maintenance, and recovery gameplay.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, single-page top-down browser prototype rather than a full 3D production game.
- Center gameplay on a UAZ-469-style scout, terrain sampling, mission stops, and workshop upgrades.
- Include simulation specifications, a vehicle roster, and a three-hour field plan in the in-game Field Manual.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built field, workshop, and Field Manual views in `index.html`, with responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented controls, terrain sampling, mission objectives, telemetry, upgrades, repairs, and recovery UI in `game.js`.
- Added drivetrain/traction influences and water-related engine and chassis wear.
- The Field Manual includes all six requested vehicle types and sections for simulation specs and first-three-hours planning.

### Active
- Finish and validate winch/recovery behavior: `findNearestRoadPoint()` and `state.winchAnchor` exist, but winch activation does not assign an anchor.
- Fix water-damage logic: `crossedLimit` is now unused, and depth is overwritten after damage checks, so verify and correct the intended ford-limit behavior.
- Replace the placeholder “TOPO MAP OPENED” response with a usable map if in scope.
- Validate CTIS, upgrades, repairs, terrain transitions, and full mission progression; re-run `node --check game.js` and browser checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire winch activation to select a suitable anchor, complete recovery behavior, and render the winch line if appropriate.
2. Correct and test ford depth and water damage behavior.
3. Validate map, CTIS, repair, upgrade effects, and mission completion in-browser; run `node --check game.js`.
4. Review the first-three-hours plan content and summarize prototype scope and simplifications.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Simulation, controls, terrain sampling, upgrades, winch, recovery, and mission logic.
- `index.html`: Game interface, workshop, and Field Manual.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and visual styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- `game.js` has `findNearestRoadPoint()` and `state.winchAnchor`, but the winch button only toggles `winchActive`; the anchor-based pull cannot work until an anchor is assigned.
- Recovery currently only displays “Recovery hook reached — reposition and retry.” The map button currently only displays “TOPO MAP OPENED.”
- The prototype is a simplified 2D top-down simulation, not production-grade deformable 3D physics.

TAIGA is a slow, systemic off-road simulation. The terrain remembers every pass; the truck remembers every mistake.

DESIGN PILLAR 01WEIGHT · GRIP · CONSEQUENCE
SIMULATION SPEC 01 / DRIVETRAIN

Torque, not horsepower.

A fixed-step, wheel-level model prioritizes controllable torque delivery. Each wheel samples local ground state and feeds load, slip, and damage back into the chassis.

01

Powertrain

Engine torque curve → clutch slip → 4-speed gearbox → selectable high/low transfer case → open / locked differentials → axle reduction → tyre contact patch. Low range multiplies wheel torque 2.7× and caps road speed.

ENGINE BRAKING · CLUTCH HEAT · STALL / RESTART

Axles & lockers

Stock civilian axles; military portal axles add +90 mm clearance with greater unsprung mass. Lockers force axle-wheel speed parity; binding on hard turns raises shaft stress. Reinforced half-shafts raise torque threshold.

OPEN → REAR LOCK → FRONT + REAR LOCK
03

Tyres & pressure

CTIS lowers pressure on the move: more footprint and flotation, but more heat, rolling drag, and bead risk. Beadlocks widen safe pressure range. Chains add snow / ice bite, reduce soft-ground flotation.

30 PSI ROAD · 18 PSI MIXED · 8 PSI BOG (LOCKED RIMS)
04

Terrain & water

Wheel load deforms a moisture-dependent soil grid. Rut depth raises drag; wheelspin polishes mud into slick clay. Peat has a shear-strength limit and can swallow a stopped vehicle. Flowing water adds lateral force and drag.

SNORKEL PROTECTS INTAKE · NOT ELECTRICS OR CABIN
05

Damage & wear

Impacts stress suspension and chassis; high RPM in mud heats clutch and engine; submerged ignition misfires. Tyre cuts bleed pressure. Field repair consumes parts and time; recovery costs cash and abandons optional cargo.

COMPONENTS: ENGINE · COOLING · AXLES · TYRES · FRAME
06

Winching

Choose an anchor, pay cable out, tension rises against vehicle mass and terrain suction. Line angle matters; trees can uproot. A high-amp winch pulls harder but draws battery current—engine off means finite reserve.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser prototype combining SnowRunner-style terrain and logistics with UAZ-style mechanical tuning and domestic vehicles.
- Deliver the upgrade tree, drivetrain simulation specifications, vehicle roster, and first-three-hours mission plan through the game experience.

## Requirements
- Include mud, peat bogs, snow, water currents, winching, component damage/wear, and recovery.
- Include granular tuning for portal axles, lockers, crawler gearing, reinforced shafts, CTIS, beadlocks, bogger tires, chains, snorkels, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lifts, and winches.
- Feature vehicles inspired by the UAZ-469, UAZ-452, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Support taiga scouting, low-gear crawling, field maintenance, and recovery gameplay.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, single-page top-down browser prototype rather than a full 3D production game.
- Center gameplay on a UAZ-469-style scout, terrain sampling, mission stops, and workshop upgrades.
- Include simulation specifications, a vehicle roster, and a three-hour field plan in the in-game Field Manual.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built field, workshop, and Field Manual views in `index.html`, with responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented controls, terrain sampling, mission objectives, telemetry, upgrades, repairs, and recovery UI in `game.js`.
- Added drivetrain/traction influences and water-related engine and chassis wear.
- The Field Manual includes all six requested vehicle types and sections for simulation specs and first-three-hours planning.
- Corrected water-depth calculation to derive depth from river proximity and updated ford-limit damage to use the computed depth.
- Added a modal topographic-map interface in `index.html` and styling in `style.css`.

### Active
- Wire winch activation to select an anchor; `state.winchAnchor` exists, but button activation still only toggles `winchActive`.
- Implement map drawing/open-close behavior; the map dialog exists but `mapToggle` still only shows “TOPO MAP OPENED.”
- Validate water-depth/ford damage, CTIS, upgrades, repairs, terrain transitions, and mission progression in-browser; run `node --check game.js`.
- Review the first-three-hours plan content and summarize prototype scope and simplifications.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement winch anchor selection, pull/cancel behavior, and visible winch line; ensure behavior is usable with and without the winch upgrade as intended.
2. Connect `mapToggle` and `mapClose` to show/hide the dialog and render route, river, objectives, and vehicle position on `topoMap`.
3. Test ford-depth damage, CTIS, upgrade effects, repair, terrain transitions, and complete mission progression; run `node --check game.js`.
4. Review the manual content and summarize the prototype’s scope and simplifications.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Simulation, controls, terrain sampling, upgrades, winch, recovery, and mission logic.
- `index.html`: Game interface, map dialog, workshop, and Field Manual.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and modal-map styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- `findNearestRoadPoint()` exists and returns `{ point, distance }`; `state.winchAnchor` exists, but no current activation code assigns it.
- `recoverBtn` still only displays “Recovery hook reached — reposition and retry.”
- The map button is not yet wired to the new modal or map rendering.
- The prototype is a simplified 2D top-down simulation, not production-grade deformable 3D physics.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser prototype combining SnowRunner-style terrain and logistics with UAZ-style mechanical tuning and domestic vehicles.
- Deliver the upgrade tree, drivetrain simulation specifications, vehicle roster, and first-three-hours mission plan through the game experience.

## Requirements
- Include mud, peat bogs, snow, water currents, winching, component damage/wear, and recovery.
- Include granular tuning for portal axles, lockers, crawler gearing, reinforced shafts, CTIS, beadlocks, bogger tires, chains, snorkels, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lifts, and winches.
- Feature vehicles inspired by the UAZ-469, UAZ-452, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Support taiga scouting, low-gear crawling, field maintenance, and recovery gameplay.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, single-page top-down browser prototype rather than a full 3D production game.
- Center gameplay on a UAZ-469-style scout, terrain sampling, mission stops, and workshop upgrades.
- Include simulation specifications, a vehicle roster, and a three-hour field plan in the in-game Field Manual.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built field, workshop, and Field Manual views in `index.html`, with responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented controls, terrain sampling, mission objectives, telemetry, upgrades, repairs, and recovery UI in `game.js`.
- Added terrain/drivetrain influences and water-related engine and chassis wear; water depth is derived from river proximity and used for ford-limit damage.
- Added a topographic map dialog showing route, river, objectives, contours, and vehicle; open/close, Escape, backdrop close, live marker updates, and redraw-on-open are wired.
- Wired winch activation to select a nearby logging-road anchor, draw a cable, pull toward it, and cancel/release; standard and upgraded ranges differ.
- Made CTIS require the CTIS upgrade and update displayed tire pressure.
- Implemented paid recovery to the nearest logging-road point.
- Field Manual contains all six requested vehicle types and sections for simulation specs and first-three-hours planning.
- Latest `node --check game.js` passed before the most recent map redraw edits.

### Active
- Validate map behavior, winch/recovery, ford damage, CTIS, upgrade effects, repairs, terrain transitions, and full mission progression in a browser.
- Re-run `node --check game.js` after the latest edits and review the manual content and simulation simplifications.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js` and browser-test map updates/close behavior, winch anchor and pull, and recovery.
2. Test water-depth/ford damage, CTIS, upgrade effects, repairs, terrain transitions, and completion of all mission stops.
3. Review the first-three-hours plan and note discrepancies between Field Manual simulation claims and the simplified prototype mechanics.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Simulation, controls, terrain sampling, upgrades, map, winch, recovery, and mission logic.
- `index.html`: Game interface, map dialog, workshop, and Field Manual.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and modal-map styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Browser validation has not yet been performed; `/usr/bin/chromium` is available, but no Playwright/Puppeteer/JS DOM package was found.
- The prototype is a simplified 2D top-down simulation, not production-grade deformable 3D physics; some Field Manual claims may exceed implemented mechanics.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser prototype combining SnowRunner-style terrain and logistics with UAZ-style mechanical tuning and domestic vehicles.
- Deliver the upgrade tree, drivetrain simulation specifications, vehicle roster, and first-three-hours mission plan through the game experience.

## Requirements
- Include mud, peat bogs, snow, water currents, winching, component damage/wear, and recovery.
- Include granular tuning for portal axles, lockers, crawler gearing, reinforced shafts, CTIS, beadlocks, bogger tires, chains, snorkels, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lifts, and winches.
- Feature vehicles inspired by the UAZ-469, UAZ-452, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Support taiga scouting, low-gear crawling, field maintenance, and recovery gameplay.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, single-page top-down browser prototype rather than a full 3D production game.
- Center gameplay on a UAZ-469-style scout, terrain sampling, mission stops, and workshop upgrades.
- Include simulation specifications, a vehicle roster, and a three-hour field plan in the in-game Field Manual.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built field, workshop, and Field Manual views in `index.html`, with responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented controls, terrain sampling, mission objectives, telemetry, upgrades, repairs, and recovery UI in `game.js`.
- Added terrain/drivetrain influences and water-related engine and chassis wear; water depth is derived from river proximity and used for ford-limit damage.
- Added a topographic map dialog showing route, river, objectives, contours, and vehicle; open/close, Escape, backdrop close, live marker updates, and redraw-on-open are wired.
- Wired winch activation to select a nearby logging-road anchor, draw a cable, pull toward it, and cancel/release; standard and upgraded ranges differ.
- Made CTIS require the CTIS upgrade and update displayed tire pressure.
- Implemented paid recovery to the nearest logging-road point.
- Field Manual contains simulation-spec and mission-plan content; review is still needed for consistency with implemented mechanics.
- `node --check game.js` passed after the latest map redraw edits.
- Browser-tested map open/focus/canvas sizing, winch anchor and pull, ford depth and damage, CTIS purchase and pressure toggle, and completion of all three mission stops; these checks passed.

### Active
- Validate recovery, upgrade effects, repairs, terrain transitions, and gameplay behavior beyond the tested mission-stop completion.
- Review whether the Field Manual contains the required complete vehicle roster and first-three-hours plan, and correct claims that exceed the simplified mechanics.
- Investigate the browser console’s 404 error from the test run.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test paid recovery, field repairs, and remaining upgrade effects in the browser.
2. Review Field Manual content against implemented mechanics and the required roster/three-hour plan; revise unsupported claims if necessary.
3. Identify and resolve the browser console 404, then rerun syntax and browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Simulation, controls, terrain sampling, upgrades, map, winch, recovery, and mission logic.
- `index.html`: Game interface, map dialog, workshop, and Field Manual.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and modal-map styling.

FIELD GUIDE 01—06

Traction is a conversation
with the ground.

TAIGA is a slow, systemic off-road simulation. The terrain remembers every pass; the truck remembers every mistake.

DESIGN PILLAR 01WEIGHT · GRIP · CONSEQUENCE
SIMULATION SPEC 01 / DRIVETRAIN

Torque, not horsepower.

A fixed-step, wheel-level model prioritizes controllable torque delivery. Each wheel samples local ground state and feeds load, slip, and damage back into the chassis.

01

Powertrain

Engine torque curve → clutch slip → 4-speed gearbox → selectable high/low transfer case → open / locked differentials → axle reduction → tyre contact patch. Low range multiplies wheel torque 2.7× and caps road speed.

ENGINE BRAKING · CLUTCH HEAT · STALL / RESTART
02

Axles & lockers

Stock civilian axles; military portal axles add +90 mm clearance with greater unsprung mass. Lockers force axle-wheel speed parity; binding on hard turns raises shaft stress. Reinforced half-shafts raise torque threshold.

OPEN → REAR LOCK → FRONT + REAR LOCK
03

Tyres & pressure

CTIS lowers pressure on the move: more footprint and flotation, but more heat, rolling drag, and bead risk. Beadlocks widen safe pressure range. Chains add snow / ice bite, reduce soft-ground flotation.

30 PSI ROAD · 18 PSI MIXED · 8 PSI BOG (LOCKED RIMS)
04

Terrain & water

Wheel load deforms a moisture-dependent soil grid. Rut depth raises drag; wheelspin polishes mud into slick clay. Peat has a shear-strength limit and can swallow a stopped vehicle. Flowing water adds lateral force and drag.

SNORKEL PROTECTS INTAKE · NOT ELECTRICS OR CABIN
05

Damage & wear

Impacts stress suspension and chassis; high RPM in mud heats clutch and engine; submerged ignition misfires. Tyre cuts bleed pressure. Field repair consumes parts and time; recovery costs cash and abandons optional cargo.

COMPONENTS: ENGINE · COOLING · AXLES · TYRES · FRAME
06

Winching

Choose an anchor, pay cable out, tension rises against vehicle mass and terrain suction. Line angle matters; trees can uproot. A high-amp winch pulls harder but draws battery current—engine off means finite reserve.

ANCHOR · CABLE · LOAD · MOTOR HEAT · BATTERY
DOMESTIC FLEET 06 CHASSIS

Built for the long way around.

01 / SCOUTUAZ-469Simple field service · modular 4×4AVAILABLE NOW
02 / VANUAZ-452 “Bukhanka”Cab-over utility · people / cargoUNLOCK · CH. 02
03 / LIGHT SCOUTVAZ-2121 NivaLight monocoque · full-time AWDUNLOCK · CH. 02
04 / MICRO-UTILITYLuAZ-969Low mass · portal hubs · tiny payloadUNLOCK · CH. 03
05 / MEDIUM TRUCKGAZ-66Portal axles · 2 t payload · recoveryUNLOCK · CH. 03
06 / HEAVY HAULUral-43206×6 torque · bridge / supply contractsUNLOCK · CH. 04
FIRST 3 HOURSFIELD PLAN
FIELD CONTROLSKEYBOARD
Steer / accelerate / reverseW A S D
Low / high rangeLH
Winch / tyre pressureQE
HandbrakeSPACE
Toggle differential lockX
THE TAIGA RULE

When the wheels stop moving, stop adding throttle.

Read the rut. Change the setup. Pull, don't spin.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser prototype combining SnowRunner-style terrain and logistics with UAZ-style mechanical tuning and domestic vehicles.
- Deliver the upgrade tree, drivetrain simulation specifications, vehicle roster, and first-three-hours mission plan through the game experience.

## Requirements
- Include mud, peat bogs, snow, water currents, winching, component damage/wear, and recovery.
- Include granular tuning for portal axles, lockers, crawler gearing, reinforced shafts, CTIS, beadlocks, bogger tires, chains, snorkels, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lifts, and winches.
- Feature vehicles inspired by the UAZ-469, UAZ-452, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Support taiga scouting, low-gear crawling, field maintenance, and recovery gameplay.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, single-page top-down browser prototype rather than a full 3D production game.
- Center gameplay on a UAZ-469-style scout, terrain sampling, mission stops, and workshop upgrades.
- Include simulation specifications, a vehicle roster, and a three-hour field plan in the in-game Field Manual.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built field, workshop, and Field Manual views in `index.html`, with responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented controls, terrain sampling, mission objectives, telemetry, upgrades, repairs, and recovery UI in `game.js`.
- Added terrain/drivetrain influences and water-related engine and chassis wear; water depth is derived from river proximity and used for ford-limit damage.
- Added a topographic map dialog with route, river, objectives, contours, vehicle marker, open/close, Escape/backdrop close, focus handling, and redraw-on-open.
- Wired winching to select a nearby logging-road anchor, draw a cable, pull toward it, and cancel/release; standard and upgraded ranges differ.
- Made CTIS require the CTIS upgrade and update displayed tire pressure; added paid recovery to the nearest logging-road point.
- Browser-tested map open/focus/canvas sizing, winch anchor and pull, ford depth and damage, CTIS purchase and pressure toggle, and completion of all three mission stops; checks passed.
- Confirmed Field Manual lists the six requested vehicle types.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Validate paid recovery, field repairs, and remaining upgrade effects; inspect discrepancies between Field Manual claims and simplified implemented mechanics.
- Populate the currently empty `#timeline` in the Field Manual with the first-three-hours plan.
- Identify the source of the browser console 404 and rerun browser checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test recovery, repairs, and upgrade effects in the browser, correcting issues found.
2. Rewrite Field Manual claims that exceed implemented mechanics and add the three-hour plan.
3. Identify the source of the browser console 404, then rerun syntax and browser validation.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Simulation, controls, terrain sampling, upgrades, map, winch, recovery, and mission logic.
- `index.html`: Game interface, map dialog, workshop, and Field Manual; contains an empty `#timeline` element.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and modal-map styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Browser testing used Playwright with `/usr/bin/chromium`; one console error occurred: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)`.
- Latest browser checks confirmed map canvas dimensions `[1008, 600]`, winch engagement at 98 m, water depth around 1.0 m at the river sample, CTIS toggling to 18 PSI, and mission progress reaching `3 / 3`.
- The Field Manual currently describes unimplemented wheel-level physics, soil deformation, detailed drivetrain behavior, and winch battery/anchor mechanics; the prototype is simplified 2D top-down simulation, not production-grade deformable 3D physics.
- Inspection found upgrade effects are unevenly implemented: portal axles, boggers, chains, transfer case, snorkel, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lift, and winch affect some stats or behavior; locker upgrades and reinforced shafts have no observed use beyond purchase metadata.

DIV spec-grid
01
Powertrain
Engine torque curve → clutch slip → 4-speed gearbox → selectable high/low transfer case → open / locked differentials → axle reduction → tyre contact patch. Low range multiplies wheel torque 2.7× and caps road speed.
ENGINE BRAKING · CLUTCH HEAT · STALL / RESTART
02
Axles & lockers
Stock civilian axles; military portal axles add +90 mm clearance with greater unsprung mass. Lockers force axle-wheel speed parity; binding on hard turns raises shaft stress. Reinforced half-shafts raise torque threshold.
OPEN → REAR LOCK → FRONT + REAR LOCK
03
Tyres & pressure
CTIS lowers pressure on the move: more footprint and flotation, but more heat, rolling drag, and bead risk. Beadlocks widen safe pressure range. Chains add snow / ice bite, reduce soft-ground flotation.
30 PSI ROAD · 18 PSI MIXED · 8 PSI BOG (LOCKED RIMS)
04
Terrain & water
Wheel load deforms a moisture-dependent soil grid. Rut depth raises drag; wheelspin polishes mud into slick clay. Peat has a shear-strength limit and can swallow a stopped vehicle. Flowing water adds lateral force and drag.
SNORKEL PROTECTS INTAKE · NOT ELECTRICS OR CABIN
05
Damage & wear
Impacts stress suspension and chassis; high RPM in mud heats clutch and engine; submerged ignition misfires. Tyre cuts bleed pressure. Field repair consumes parts and time; recovery costs cash and abandons optional cargo.
COMPONENTS: ENGINE · COOLING · AXLES · TYRES · FRAME
06
Winching
Choose an anchor, pay cable out, tension rises against vehicle mass and terrain suction. Line angle matters; trees can uproot. A high-amp winch pulls harder but draws battery current—engine off means finite reserve.
ANCHOR · CABLE · LOAD · MOTOR HEAT · BATTERY

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser prototype combining SnowRunner-style terrain and logistics with UAZ-style mechanical tuning and domestic vehicles.
- Deliver the upgrade tree, drivetrain simulation specifications, vehicle roster, and first-three-hours mission plan through the game experience.

## Requirements
- Include mud, peat bogs, snow, water currents, winching, component damage/wear, and recovery.
- Include granular tuning for portal axles, lockers, crawler gearing, reinforced shafts, CTIS, beadlocks, bogger tires, chains, snorkels, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lifts, and winches.
- Feature vehicles inspired by the UAZ-469, UAZ-452, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Support taiga scouting, low-gear crawling, field maintenance, and recovery gameplay.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, single-page top-down browser prototype rather than a full 3D production game.
- Center gameplay on a UAZ-469-style scout, terrain sampling, mission stops, and workshop upgrades.
- Include simulation specifications, a vehicle roster, and a three-hour field plan in the in-game Field Manual.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built field, workshop, and Field Manual views in `index.html`, with responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented controls, terrain sampling, mission objectives, telemetry, upgrades, repairs, and recovery UI in `game.js`.
- Added terrain/drivetrain influences and water-related engine and chassis wear; water depth is derived from river proximity and used for ford-limit damage.

01—06
Traction is a conversation

TAIGA is a slow, systemic off-road simulation. The terrain remembers every pass; the truck remembers every mistake.
DESIGN PILLAR 01

01 / DRIVETRAIN
Torque, not horsepower.

01
Powertrain

Axles & lockers

OPEN → REAR LOCK → FRONT + REAR LOCK

Tyres & pressure
CTIS lowers pressure on the move: more footprint and flotation, but more heat, rolling drag, and bead risk. Beadlocks widen safe pressure range. Chains add snow / ice bite, reduce soft-ground flotation.
30 PSI ROAD · 18 PSI MIXED · 8 PSI BOG (LOCKED RIMS)
04
Terrain & water
Wheel load deforms a moisture-dependent soil grid. Rut depth raises drag; wheelspin polishes mud into slick clay. Peat has a shear-strength limit and can swallow a stopped vehicle. Flowing water adds lateral force and drag.
SNORKEL PROTECTS INTAKE · NOT ELECTRICS OR CABIN
05
Damage & wear
Impacts stress suspension and chassis; high RPM in mud heats clutch and engine; submerged ignition misfires. Tyre cuts bleed pressure. Field repair consumes parts and time; recovery costs cash and abandons optional cargo.

Winching
Choose an anchor, pay cable out, tension rises against vehicle mass and terrain suction. Line angle matters; trees can uproot. A high-amp winch pulls harder but draws battery current—engine off means finite reserve.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable browser prototype combining SnowRunner-style terrain and logistics with UAZ-style mechanical tuning and domestic vehicles.
- Deliver the upgrade tree, drivetrain simulation specifications, vehicle roster, and first-three-hours mission plan through the game experience.

## Requirements
- Include mud, peat bogs, snow, water currents, winching, component damage/wear, and recovery.
- Include granular tuning for portal axles, lockers, crawler gearing, reinforced shafts, CTIS, beadlocks, bogger tires, chains, snorkels, sealed ignition, radiator relocation, suspension lifts, and winches.
- Feature vehicles inspired by the UAZ-469, UAZ-452, VAZ-2121 Niva, LuAZ-969, GAZ-66, and Ural.
- Support taiga scouting, low-gear crawling, field maintenance, and recovery gameplay.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained, single-page top-down browser prototype rather than a full 3D production game.
- Center gameplay on a UAZ-469-style scout, terrain sampling, mission stops, and workshop upgrades.
- Include simulation specifications, a vehicle roster, and a three-hour field plan in the in-game Field Manual.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built field, workshop, and Field Manual views in `index.html`, with responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Implemented controls, terrain sampling, mission objectives, telemetry, upgrades, repairs, and recovery UI in `game.js`.
- Added terrain/drivetrain influences and water-related engine and chassis wear; water depth is derived from river proximity and used for ford-limit damage.
- Added a topographic map dialog with route, river, objectives, contours, vehicle marker, open/close, Escape/backdrop close, focus handling, and redraw-on-open.
- Wired winching to select a nearby logging-road anchor, draw a cable, pull toward it, and cancel/release; standard and upgraded ranges differ.
- Made CTIS require the CTIS upgrade and update displayed tire pressure; added paid recovery to the nearest logging-road point.
- Browser-tested map open/focus/canvas sizing, winch anchor and pull, ford depth and damage, CTIS purchase and pressure toggle, and completion of all three mission stops; checks passed.
- Confirmed Field Manual lists the six requested vehicle types.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Began wiring tangible upgrade effects in `getVehicleStats()`; equipped lockers now modify locked-differential traction, crawler transfer case modifies low-range acceleration, and stats now expose shaft shock protection and beadlock low-pressure tire-wear multiplier (the latter two are not yet applied in simulation).

### Active
- Finish integrating and validating upgrade effects, particularly reinforced shafts, beadlocks, and front/rear lockers; ensure upgrade descriptions match real behavior.
- Populate the currently empty `#timeline` in the Field Manual with the first-three-hours plan.
- Rewrite overstated Field Manual simulation claims to match the prototype’s simplified terrain sampling and vehicle-level traction/damage rather than wheel-level physics, soil deformation, detailed drivetrain behavior, or winch battery/anchor mechanics.
- Investigate the browser console 404 and rerun browser checks, including paid recovery and field repairs.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Apply the new `shockProtection` and `tireWearMultiplier` stats in `updateState()` and check that lockers have accurate descriptions/controls.
2. Add the three-hour mission plan to `#timeline` and revise the Field Manual’s simulation claims.
3. Diagnose the 404, then rerun syntax and browser validation for recovery, repairs, and upgrade effects.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Simulation, controls, terrain sampling, upgrades, map, winch, recovery, and mission logic.
- `index.html`: Game interface, map dialog, workshop, and Field Manual; contains an empty `#timeline` element.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and modal-map styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Browser testing used Playwright with `/usr/bin/chromium`; one console error occurred: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)`.
- Latest browser checks confirmed map canvas dimensions `[1008, 600]`, winch engagement at 98 m, water depth around 1.0 m at the river sample, CTIS toggling to 18 PSI, and mission progress reaching `3 / 3`.
- The most recent edit changed `getVehicleStats()` in `game.js`, but has not been tested; its new shaft and tire-wear stats are not yet consumed by simulation logic.

04
Terrain & water
Wheel load deforms a moisture-dependent soil grid. Rut depth raises drag; wheelspin polishes mud into slick clay. Peat has a shear-strength limit and can swallow a stopped vehicle. Flowing water adds lateral force and drag.
SNORKEL PROTECTS INTAKE · NOT ELECTRICS OR CABIN
05
Damage & wear
Impacts stress suspension and chassis; high RPM in mud heats clutch and engine; submerged ignition misfires. Tyre cuts bleed pressure. Field repair consumes parts and time; recovery costs cash and abandons optional cargo.

06
Winching
Choose an anchor, pay cable out, tension rises against vehicle mass and terrain suction. Line angle matters; trees can uproot. A high-amp winch pulls harder but draws battery current—engine off means finite reserve.
